what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission walked a town forest to review a finished timber harvest; no votes were taken.
The consulting forester explained the harvest, the new parking area, the gate and landing, and the reason for cutting around hemlock.
Net timber proceeds were described as going into Conservation Commission funds for parking, trail markers and pollinator gardens.
The forester described hemlock woolly adelgid and forest regeneration while the group walked the property.
Some sale revenue may go toward finishing boundary identification on the west side of the property.

why_it_matters: Money from the town-owned timber sale goes to the Conservation Commission's funds for local trails, parking and boundary work, so it is not part of a tax-funded budget request in this meeting.
The forest's hemlock health and boundary marking affect how the land is kept and used, and any later spending of the proceeds would come before the Commission.
